title: Adaptive SLO-based pager filtering and automated runbook execution for multi-region failures
creator: Mariana Gupta
description:
Goal: Reduce noisy pages while preserving fast response for real customer-impacting incidents during multi-region degradations. Implement adaptive pager filtering driven by SLO burn rates and region-aware circuit-breaker state, plus automated runbook triggers for known failure modes. The feature should integrate with the Console alerting pipeline (Grafana/Alertmanager), the incident response automation engine, and our on-call runbooks stored in Confluence.

Scope:
- Define SLO-derived alert thresholds and burn-rate windows for service-level and system-level SLOs.
- Implement an Alertrouter shim that annotates alerts with SLO context and circuit-breaker status and applies suppression/throttling rules.
- Automate runbook execution for 3 canonical failure modes: cross-region latency spike, KV cache invalidation, and model-variant fallback loops.
- Add telemetry: suppressed-alert metrics, pager-rate by SLO cohort, false-positive rate estimate.

Non-goals: Full rewrite of Alertmanager, replacing existing paging provider.
acceptance_criteria: Pager rate reduced by >=50% for non-customer-impacting SLO burns in staging tests
SLO burn annotation present on all matching alerts and visible in Console alert details
Automated runbook executes playbook tasks for the three canonical failure modes and creates/update the incident ticket
Documentation and on-call runbooks reviewed and signed off by oncall rotation and SRE lead
End-to-end e2e test that simulates a regional outage and validates circuit-breaker-triggered routing and automated runbook behavior
activities: 2026-03-10 - Ticket created by Mariana Gupta: initial proposal and scope. Linked RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Reliability/Adaptive+Pager+Filtering+RFC
2026-03-11 - Spike: Liam ran a small PoC that annotated alerts with slo.burn_rate and region tags. Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/alert-router/pull/281
2026-03-12 - Design review with SRE and Console teams. Decision: Use an injectable Alertrouter shim to avoid Alertmanager fork. Action: ENG-19902 created to add routing hook in Console
2026-03-13 - Implemented suppression rules prototype (PR 289). Observed 60% reduction in staging pager volume for low-priority alerts.

2026-03-13 - Added automated runbook stub: runbook executor triggers Slack playbooks and populates Linear incidents. Demo run recorded: https://drives.redwood.ai/drive/folders/0B_runbooks/demo-2026-03-13
2026-03-14 - QA: Integration tests failing under high-concurrency; suspected race in runbook executor. Assigned to Liam for fix.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: suppressing alerts risks missing signal; mitigation is to only suppress when SLO burn is transient (<5m) or when circuit-breaker state indicates graceful degradation.
We're using conservative defaults for initial rollout: only suppress P3/P2 and route P0/P1 to immediate paging.
Need follow-up: map customer-facing SLOs to alert cohorts (PM and Support input required). See PM ticket: PM-726
Related dashboards: Grafana board 'Pager Noise & SLOs' (dashboards/board/19).
Runbook automation will require short-lived service token with scoped permissions; security to review before prod rollout.
